espn-604005.headline: Twice in a row to England has happened once before
beats: The last and only time New Zealand lost successive Tests to England was 2002-03, with a World Cup looming. England won the last meeting 33–19, on 15 November 2025. New Zealand's next game after this one is at a World Cup.

New Zealand arrive from a 28–35 defeat in Wales, after which Dave Rennie said they "let ourselves down and let our country down". England have won four straight, the latest 78–15 against Japan. Will Joseph scored five tries that day and is in line for a third cap.

Rennie hopes to have Will Jordan back on the wing after a knee problem kept him out in Cardiff. England weighed Freddie Steward's aerial game against Jordan and Jordie Barrett, but are expected to keep George Furbank at full-back.
An England win by 16 or more lifts them to third in the world and drops New Zealand to fifth, two places below them. That would also be twice in a row.

espn-604006.headline: Seven Scots out, and Japan still counting to 78
beats: Captain Sione Tuipulotu is one of seven players gone from Scotland's squad. Jack Dempsey, who faces surgery after a foot injury, plays his club rugby at Toshiba Brave Lupus, so the Scot who sees most of Japanese rugby is out as well.

Gregor Townsend was already planning changes to simulate scenarios for next year's World Cup, with a new kilted Kiwi in line for a Test debut. The rehearsal now has a thinner cast, and Rory Darge, who led the side against Australia, keeps the armband in all but name.
Scotland beat Australia 15–12 in an arm wrestle Townsend rated among their best defensive performances in recent years. Japan ran Wales to 28–21, then conceded 13 tries in a 78–15 defeat in England.
A Japan win would lift them above Italy in the world rankings, which is who Scotland play next, in February.

espn-604007.headline: Erasmus plans to watch this one from his hotel
beats: Rassie Erasmus is serving a six-match ban for questioning the integrity of the officials after South Africa's 21–19 defeat by France in Paris. SA Rugby have asked for a full hearing, but his absence from the Aviva looks certain either way. He has invited supporters to watch it with him online instead.
He did call one decision correctly. He predicted Sam Prendergast would be cleared of the hip-drop citing from the Fiji game, and the Ireland fly-half is free to play.

That leaves two former Ireland players, Felix Jones and Jerry Flannery, with more of the say against their old side. South Africa won 24–13 on this ground last November. Since then, Ireland have put 42 on Argentina and 43 on Fiji at home.
Hanyani Shimange expects the ban to make the Springboks angrier, not weaker. Any Ireland win takes them off the top of the world rankings, which is a lot to watch from a hotel room.

espn-604008.headline: Six wins each, and none yet in this competition
beats: Italy and Fiji have met 12 times and won six apiece, the last an Italy win in Catania, 19–10, in November 2017. Nine years on, neither has won in five Nations Championship games, and each sits last in its conference.

Italy let a strong first half-hour against Argentina drift into a 14–19 home defeat. Simone Ferrari says it burns and that those errors cannot happen again. Fiji have conceded 54 and 43 in a fortnight, to France and Ireland.
Ferrari calls Italy's scrum a well-honed weapon. Their breakdown coach German Fernandez warns that Fiji love to play in chaos. Win, and Italy go above Fiji to 10th in the world.
Italy are already bound for the 11th-place final on 27 November, and Fiji probably are too. If so, the loser gets five days to work out what went wrong, then plays the same side again.

espn-604009.headline: One point clear of England, with Argentina left to play
beats: France beat South Africa 21–19 on 13 November and top the North by a point from England with one pool round left. Laurent Sempéré said they treated these three autumn games as one block, aimed at Twickenham, where the final is played.

Argentina come off a 19–14 win in Italy that looked little like a warm-up for Paris. Both sides gave away 16 penalties, and Argentina played seven minutes with 13 men after yellow cards to Sclavi and Elias. Sempéré was also asked about Shaun Edwards, who is now working with Argentina.
France have Matthieu Jalibert back in the squad after nearly two months out with a torn right quadriceps. An Argentina win would drop France to fourth in the world, below Ireland.
Argentina cannot catch South Africa for second in the South. They can still make France's road to Twickenham longer.

espn-604010.headline: The hard part for Wales was supposed to be last week
beats: Wales beat New Zealand 35–28 in Cardiff on 14 November, with five tries and a record number of tackles. Steve Tandy is now considering changes for Australia, who arrive on four straight defeats.

James Botham, Player of the Match with 30 tackles, could miss it for the birth of his child. Matt Sherratt's view of his flanker: "Jim does come to the party when there's a big game." This one may have to be a smaller party.
Australia conceded 50, 43 and 45 in three of those four losses, then held Scotland to 15 and still lost by three. Win by 16 or more and Wales go above them to eighth in the world.
Wales go to France in February. Australia's next Test after this is Hong Kong at the World Cup, which is a long time to sit on a fifth straight defeat.
